sentences.text: Appearance:

Shri Tarun Kushwah, learned counsel for the applican  Shri Rahul Solanki, learned Govt.Advocate for the re  Shri Manoj Malviya, learned counsel for the objector  ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (in short "B.N.S.S."), for grant of bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.237/2024 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Sailana, District Ratlam (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 376(2)(N), 450, 506 of IPC.
2.
Prosecution story, in brief, is that on 5.6.2024 at around 8.00 PM when the prosecutrix was inside of her parent's house, the applicant entered in her room and committed rape upon her.
He threatened her that if she narrates the incident to anyone, he will kill her.
After some days he again repeated the aforesaid act.
The matter was reported on 5.6.2024.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23291 2 MCRC-34779-2024 3.
Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that the prosecutrix is a major lady aged around 24 years.
She was consenting party for sexual intercourse, but when her husband saw the incident, he pressurized the prosecutrix to lodge report.
Then, she lodged report against the applicant.

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 5.6.2024.

After completion of investigation,
charge-sheet has been filed.

Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal,
therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of the bail application.
5. Learned counsel for the objector pleaded that he has no objection if the applicant is granted bail.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail hence, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant - Vikram shall be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23291 3 MCRC-34779-2024 with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
8. This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
9. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
